correctness.rationale: For every n>=4, a maximal independent set has cyclic gaps 2 or 3; a legal exchange must insert adjacent to the removed vertex because it must dominate that vertex. Such slides interchange adjacent unlike gaps. Every boundary contributes a distinct edge, yielding degree 2r for r circular runs of each symbol. Counting positive run compositions, marked run starts and distinguished chosen vertices gives exact multiplicity n/r*C(a-1,r-1)*C(b-1,r-1). Vandermonde yields edge count. Sorting nonwrap gaps while fixing an anchor and exchanging boundary gaps at the anchor proves mixed-sector connectivity. Pure sectors are 2 or 3 isolated configurations. Direct exhaustive all-jump implementation passed n=4..18; independent cyclic-gap C++ verifier passed n=4..22; finite evidence supplements but does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: Closest accessible primary classification arxiv:2303.08190 covers only minimum independent dominating sets; the present complete all-cardinality component and degree laws, in particular unbounded degrees on connected nonminimum sectors, do not follow from that result. arxiv:1403.0359 and arxiv:2203.16861 permit nonmaximal intermediate independent sets and their structure does not directly imply that of the induced maximal-only subgraph. arxiv:math/0207100 concerns extremal counts, not moves. Six actual published-finding corpus semantic queries for aliases, gap words, domination, cycle reconfiguration, matchings and degree distribution found no containing implication, only unrelated nearest records. Circular runs enumeration is classical and explicitly credited. Unindexed equivalent results remain possible.

value.rationale: A complete, mathematically natural infinite-family classification rather than isolated data or an arbitrary slice: all maximal independent dominating configurations on labelled cycles, all equal-cardinality legal exchanges, every connected component and degree multiplicity, edge count and explicit frozen sectors. Nonminimum connected sectors of cycles C_(5m) with k=2m have every even degree from 2 to 2m, giving arbitrarily high local mobility, a qualitative distinction from minimum-only i-graphs. The exact result can inform move counting, constrained stochastic chains and the comparison of independent set and dominating set reconfiguration.
